seo.title: U.S. Dairy Exports by Country: Cheese, Milk Powder, Whey & Tariffs
seo.shortDescription: The U.S. exported $7.87 billion of dairy, eggs and honey in 2025, a third of it to Mexico. Who buys U.S. cheese, milk powder and whey, and what each charges.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$7.87 billion** of dairy products, eggs and honey (HS Chapter 04) in 2025, up **16.4%** from 2024. **Cheese** is the largest group at **$3.00 billion (38%)**, followed by **milk powder** ($2.11 billion, $1.92 billion of it skim milk powder), **whey** ($929 million), **eggs** ($744 million, including $471 million of hatching eggs) and **butter** ($596 million, up 153%). **Mexico** buys a third of it ($2.57 billion), mostly milk powder and cheese; Canada, South Korea, Japan and the Philippines follow. Exports are up **9.5%** in January–August 2026.

Tariffs are low in most big markets. Mexico, Australia and Colombia take U.S. dairy duty-free under trade agreements, South Korea's tariff on U.S. cheese reached **0%** in January 2026, and the Philippines charges 0–7%. Two buyers charge extra. **Canada** lets most U.S. dairy in free only within its CUSMA quotas (about 200–300% above them) and, since **September 8, 2026**, adds a **25%** counter-tariff on U.S. cheese and **50%** on milk powder, whey and honey. **China** adds its 2018–19 counter-tariffs and an extra 10% to its normal rate, so whey pays **37%** (12% with an exclusion) and cheese **45.5%**. Japan still charges 13% on U.S. hard cheese, falling to zero by 2033. Plant listings and sanitary certificates often decide who can ship at all.

keyTakeaways: Cheese, milk powder and whey are 77% of the chapter; eggs ($744 million) and butter ($596 million) grew fastest in 2025.
Mexico is a third of the business and duty-free under USMCA; Australia, Colombia and the Dominican Republic are also free, and Korea's tariff on U.S. cheese reached 0% in 2026.

Canada and China are the costly buyers: Canada's September 2026 counter-tariffs add 25% on cheese and 50% on milk powder, whey and honey on top of its quota system, and China charges 37% on whey, or 12% with an exclusion valid to December 31, 2026.
Before shipping, line up the USDA AMS dairy sanitary certificate and, for China, the EU, Chile, India and the UK, the plant's place on an FDA export list; dairy needs no Commerce export licence.
